The 300-sample SuperCon slice is dominated at high Tc by cuprates. After parsing every formula to atomic fractions and keeping only compositions that (i) use the allowed elements and (ii) have **≤ 4 elements**, the ranking is unambiguous:

| Tc (K) | Formula | Elements |
|--------|---------|----------|
| **126** | **Ba2Ca2Cu3O** | Ba, Ca, Cu, O |
| 100 | Ca0.285Sr0.665Cu1O2 | Ca, Sr, Cu, O |
| ~93 | YBa2Cu3O7±δ | Y, Ba, Cu, O |
| 35 | La2CuO4 | La, Cu, O |

Everything above 126 K in the file is illegal here: H2S (185 K; H/S not allowed) and HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8 (132 K; Hg not allowed, 5 elements). Bi-2223 / Tl-1223 need 5+ cations.

Ba2Ca2Cu3O is the 1223 cuprate (same cation skeleton as record Hg-1223, with Cu as the charge reservoir). Atomic fractions from Ba2Ca2Cu3O:

- Ba : 2/8 = 0.25 ≤ 0.333333
- Ca : 2/8 = 0.25 ≤ 0.272727
- Cu : 3/8 = 0.375 ≤ 0.454545
- O : 1/8 = 0.125 ≤ 0.697674

Tree models trained on these 300 points put a sharp maximum on this point (~110–126 K) and score nearby Ba–Ca–Cu–O stoichiometries next; YBCO-like and infinite-layer (Sr,Ca)CuO2 sit ~10–30 K lower; Fe–As, borides, and Nb/C alloys are far below.

So the composition that maximizes Tc under the 4-element cap is this 1223 cuprate.

Final: O=0.125, Cu=0.375, Ba=0.25, Ca=0.25
